t:
(a) Actions by Administrator.—The Administrator may—
        (1) participate in the technical group described in Article 7 of the Convention, and in any other body convened pursuant to the Convention for the consideration of new or additional controls on antifouling systems; 
        (2) evaluate any risks of adverse effects on nontarget organisms or human health presented by a given antifouling system such that the amendment of annex 1 of the Convention may be warranted; 
        (3) undertake an assessment of relevant environmental, technical, and economic considerations necessary to evaluate any proposals for new or additional controls of antifouling systems under the Convention, including benefits in the United States and elsewhere associated with the production and use in the United States and elsewhere, of the subject antifouling system; and 
        (4) develop recommendations based on that assessment.  
    (b) Referrals to Technical Group.—
        (1) Convening of shipping coordinating committee.—On referral of any antifouling system to the technical group described in article 7 of the Convention for consideration of new or additional controls, the Secretary of State shall convene a public meeting of the Shipping Coordinating Committee for the purpose of receiving information and comments regarding controls on such antifouling system. The Secretary of State shall publish advance notice of such meeting in the Federal Register and on the State Department’s Web site. The Administrator shall assemble and maintain a public docket containing notices pertaining to that meeting, any comments responding to those notices, the minutes of that meeting, and materials presented at that meeting. 
        (2) Report by technical group.—The Administrator shall promptly make any report by the technical group described in the Convention available to the public through the docket 
established pursuant to subsection (b) and announce the availability of that report in the Federal Register. The Administrator shall provide an opportunity for public comment on the report for a period of not less than 30 days from the time the availability of the report is announced in the Federal Register. 
        (3) Consideration of comments.—To the extent practicable, the Administrator shall take any comments into consideration in developing recommendations under subsection (a).

fable.w: The tempting wrong reading focuses on subsection (a), where the Administrator may "participate" in the Convention's technical group; that is a federal official acting, not outside participation. Subsection (b), however, requires a public meeting of the Shipping Coordinating Committee with advance Federal Register notice, a public docket, and a public comment period of at least 30 days. The Administrator must then consider those comments when developing recommendations, so the general public is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: The Administrator shall provide an opportunity for public comment on the report for a period of not less than 30 days from the time the availability of the report is announced in the Federal Register.

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly requires the Secretary of State to convene a 'public meeting' and publish notice in the Federal Register to receive information and comments from the public. It also mandates a 30-day period for 'public comment' on reports. These are clear instances of participation by people outside the federal government in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of State shall convene a public meeting of the Shipping Coordinating Committee for the purpose of receiving information and comments regarding controls on such antifouling system. The Secretary of State shall publish advance notice of such meeting in the Federal Register and on the State Department’s Web site.

opus.w: The section requires a public comment period of at least 30 days, a public meeting of the Shipping Coordinating Committee to receive information and comments, and consideration of those comments before the Administrator issues recommendations. This brings the general public, who are outside the federal government, into a federal decision. Reading 'participate' in subsection (a)(1) as only federal involvement in an international body misses the clear public comment and meeting requirements in subsection (b).
opus.s:
The Administrator shall provide an opportunity for public comment on the report for a period of not less than 30 days from the time the availability of the report is announced in the Federal Register. 
        (3) Consideration of comments.—To the extent practicable, the Administrator shall take any comments into consideration in developing recommendations under subsection (a).
opus.b: The tempting wrong reading is that subsection (a) is about the Administrator "participating" in an international technical group, which is federal officials acting abroad, not outsiders taking part in a federal decision. That fails because subsection (b) goes further. It requires a public meeting with notice in the Federal Register, a public docket, a public comment period of at least 30 days, and consideration of those comments when the Administrator develops the U.S. recommendations.

qwen_chat.w: The section explicitly requires the Secretary of State to convene a 'public meeting' to receive information and comments from the public. It also requires publishing notice in the Federal Register and maintaining a public docket. This constitutes participation by the general public (outsiders) in the federal decision-making process regarding antifouling systems.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of State shall convene a public meeting of the Shipping Coordinating Committee for the purpose of receiving information and comments regarding controls on such antifouling system. The Secretary of State shall publish advance notice of such meeting in the Federal Register and on the State Department’s Web site.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Shipping Coordinating Committee" is an internal federal body or that the "technical group" is an international body not subject to U.S. statutory participation definitions. However, the text explicitly mandates a "public meeting" and a "public comment period" for the general public, which clearly involves outsiders.
